alignments.note: זָרַם 'sweep away as a flood' rendered by the whole verb phrase 'Thou carriest ... away as with a flood'; the subject pronoun is the verb's under rule 17, 'away' completes the sweeping (rule 44), and 'as with a flood' is the ASV's rendering of the verb's own flood lexeme rather than a supplied adjunct. Discontinuous around the object suffix's 'them' (rule 25). Headed on the lexical verb 'carriest' under rule 24; the competing head is 'flood', which writes the lexeme most literally (rule 44 light-verb reasoning).
Bare predicate noun שֵׁנָה construed as a comparison; the supplied 'as' is the noun's under rule 33 and the 'a' is its own under rule 15.

יִהְיוּ 'they are', realized twice by the ASV across the two clauses it splits the line into ('they are as a sleep ... they are like grass'); under rule 34/25 the second 'they are' is the one written verb realized again, headed on the first occurrence. Competing reading: treat the second clause as verbless, giving 'are' to the כְּ under rule 49 and marking the second 'they' added under rule 25's finite-verb-inflection sentence.
Assimilated article on חָצִיר; the ASV writes bare 'grass' with no 'the' (rule 12).
Relative 'which' supplied over a finite clause juxtaposed to the written antecedent 'grass'; no relative or waw stands in the Hebrew, so rule 55 marks it added.
יַחֲלֹף 'sprouts up' → 'groweth up'; 'up' completes the lexeme of springing up (rule 44) and stays with the verb.

review_notes: Second 'they are' read as the distributed realization of the one written יִהְיוּ (rule 34) rather than a supplied copula on כְּ with an added pronoun; the alternative is named in the unit note.
'as with a flood' kept inside the verb's unit as the ASV's rendering of זָרַם's own lexeme; head on 'carriest' with 'flood' as the competing head.
